answer: We bind every agent to one human with a physical key. A foundry stamps a ferrous slug around a secure element, ships it to a bonded wharf where a notary hands it over in person, and the holder taps it in a sealed room inside a karst limestone vault to sign one keypair that becomes the identity. Reuse the slug and the vault flags the shared device fingerprint, slashing the 0.05 ETH bond behind it. Faking 10,000 agents takes 10,000 real people at the dock, about $580k in slugs, fees and bonds, plus nine days each. Picture a shipping manifest where every crate carries a named owner.
